bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USD1 has issuer-native issuance on Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Tron. Ethereum and BNB also expose separate Chainlink CCIP Burn/Mint pools, while Solana, Plume, Monad, Mantle, Morph, Aptos, AB Chain, Tempo, and X Layer are cataloged CCIP representations. The current Chainlink directory also identifies Creditcoin token 0x111111d2bf19e43c34263401e0cad979ed1cdb61 and Burn/Mint pool 0xC2eAfBAD518849e9A5Acd33E687EeAc7306C1dea, but creditcoin is not a registered Pharos chain ID, so that bridge-only deployment remains an explicit uncatalogued coverage gap. The CCIP pools and their owners, external minters, rate-limit admins, and route machinery remain Bridge Risk; they do not turn the canonical token deployments into bridge-only representations. The profile therefore remains external-validated-network.

routes.protocol: World Liberty Financial native USD1 with Chainlink CCIP
routes.reviewNote: The Ethereum USD1 deployment is issuer-native: its TokenGovernor has independent native MINTER_ROLE members and the CCIP pools use the distinct BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE. The current pool 0x36a72eD0096B414521C45E3ddC9ed657d1D9c141 and still-authorized legacy pool 0xf9e47d3720d5142930444ae6773c7f6d05696228 are bridge machinery assessed through Bridge Risk controls, not evidence that all Ethereum USD1 supply is CCIP-originated.

routes.protocol: World Liberty Financial native USD1 with Chainlink CCIP
routes.reviewNote: The BNB USD1 deployment is issuer-native: its independent TokenGovernor has native MINTER_ROLE members and the BNB CCIP pool 0xCe3f7378aE409e1CE0dD6fFA70ab683326b73f04 is the sole BRIDGE_MINTER_OR_BURNER_ROLE member. The native token deployment and its CCIP transfer rail are therefore scored in separate modules.

On-chain reads via TronGrid show this is the issuer's own TransparentUpgradeableProxy TRC20 (name 'World Liberty Financial USD', 18 decimals, implementation TTuTMNMSCAfGNfAsEMn4JbvFQx9UEPmZCA, EIP-1967 admin TKk4R4sjAhKij7NNTpvmnGq9bCpNPiSQeW, owner contract TBZbFrVxJ8uoRQUwGSFXucpa8i2aXzGqJ8), the same issuer-controlled deployment pattern as the canonical Ethereum token, not a bridge representation. World Liberty Financial's current CCIP route matrix does not list Tron, so Tron supply is issuer-minted directly and no bridge control carries the claim.

controls.label: USD1 Ethereum current CCIP Burn/Mint pool
controls.capDescription: The HybridWithExternalMinter pool's releaseOrMint path invokes the USD1 TokenGovernor external minter. The pool exposes bridge-specific lock/burn and release/mint accounting; no global token cap is inferred from the pool.

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The pool routes through CCIP Router 0x80226fc0ee2b096224eeac085bb9a8cba1146f7d; remote-peer and RMN configuration remain protocol-level controls.
routeChecks.rateLimits: getRateLimitAdmin() returned the 3-of-6 Safe 0x0D190B74308669E8f4fE7DBCe3466169B285289d; the fixed-block read did not establish a global aggregate cap.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Ethereum block 25770446, pool owner() returned 0x44835bBBA9D40DEDa9b64858095EcFB2693c9449, a contract with bytecode but no verified source or reliable public Safe/account ABI; no threshold is assigned.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: The pool's bridge accounting is distinct from native issuance and calls the external minter; route-level conservation is not treated as a native cap.
